resolutions.researcher_notes: Searched the FERC EA (CP15-144-000-EA.pdf), the FERC Notice of Availability of the EA (CP15-144-000-Notice.pdf / Federal Register 2016-01233), and the original 2015 Notice of Application (Federal Register 2015-08871) for the recorded Capacity value of 50,000 MMBtu/d. None state that figure. All three consistently state the project's purpose is to support a firm delivery of 15,000 MMBtu/d requiring the new facilities, PLUS an additional 60,000 MMBtu/d delivered using existing capacity (no new facilities needed) -- a combined total of approximately 75,000 MMBtu/d described in the EA/Notice purpose-and-need sections. Also checked oilandgaswatch.org/pipeline/6491 (JS-rendered, no static content retrievable) and Kinder Morgan/Energy Transfer investor materials via web search -- no hit on 50,000 MMBtu/d for this project. CONTRADICTION FLAG: the recorded Capacity (50,000 MMBtu/d) does not match either component (15,000 or 60,000) or the total (75,000) stated in the primary FERC filings for this exact project (Docket CP15-144, Jacksonville Expansion Project). Not a rounding-level gap -- routing to orchestrator rather than forcing a REFS_ADDED with a value the sources don't actually state.

verifications.note: EA states the Jacksonville Expansion Project includes 'approximately 3.0 miles of 30-inch-diameter looping pipeline...in Suwannee and Columbia Counties' (Branford Loop) and 'approximately 5.7 miles of 20-inch-diameter looping pipeline...in Bradford and Clay Counties' (Jacksonville Loop) -- matches recorded '20, 30' in exactly.

FERC Notice of Application (docket CP15-144-000) for the Jacksonville Expansion Project states FGT requests authorization for '(1) Approximately 3.0 miles of 30-inch mainline loop extension (Branford Loop)...(4) approximately 5.7 miles of 20-inch loop extension (Jacksonville Loop)'.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Both dual diameters (20 in and 30 in) confirmed exactly as recorded, tied to the two named loop segments that make up this project.

verifications.note: EA: FGT 'requests authorization to construct about 8.7 miles of natural gas pipeline...to provide a total of approximately 75,000 MMBtu/d of natural gas capacity' for the Jacksonville Expansion Project.
Notice of Application: FGT application under NGA section 7(c) for facilities providing 'firm transportation' of natural gas, all known as its Jacksonville Expansion Project.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Confirmed as a natural-gas pipeline project in both FERC filings.

verifications.note: EA: 'FGT requests authorization to construct about 8.7 miles of natural gas pipeline' for the Jacksonville Expansion Project, broken out as 3.0 mi (30-in Branford Loop) + 5.7 mi (20-in Jacksonville Loop) = 8.7 mi total.
Notice of Application gives the same two segment lengths (3.0 mi + 5.7 mi) for the same project.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Both FERC filings put total new pipe at 8.7 mi (3.0 + 5.7), against a recorded LengthKnown of 9.00 mi -- a 0.3 mi / ~3.4% gap, consistent with 'about 8.7 miles' rounding up to 9. Treating as corroborating within rounding per the sweep's tolerance rule; flagging the exact gap here rather than silently matching it.

verifications.note: 'Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC (FGT)...filed...an application...requesting authorization to construct, own, and operate' the Jacksonville Expansion Project facilities -- matches recorded Owner1 'Florida Gas Transmission Co LLC' at 100%.
Energy Transfer's current asset-portal page lists 'Florida Gas Transmission' as one of its pipeline entities, confirming FGT's present-day corporate identity as owner/operator.

resolutions.researcher_notes: FERC's own applicant-of-record for this docket is Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC, seeking authority to 'construct, own, and operate' the facilities -- corroborated by the current Energy Transfer asset listing naming the same entity.

No cost figure for the Jacksonville Expansion Project (Docket CP15-144) turned up in the FERC EA (its cover-sheet 'Cost:' field is blank), the Notice of Application, the Notice of Availability, web search of Energy Transfer/Kinder Morgan investor materials, or SEC EDGAR full-text search ('Jacksonville Expansion' returns zero 10-K/10-Q hits; the one Energy Transfer 10-Q pulled up by a generic web hit does not mention Jacksonville or FGT at all). TRAP AVOIDED: a Florida PSC filing (psc.state.fl.us/library/filings/2019/03697-2019) DOES contain a '$59 million' figure for something called the 'Jacksonville Expansion Project' -- but on inspection that is a completely different, unrelated Peoples Gas System (Tampa Electric) LOCAL DISTRIBUTION project from 2019 (a new 16-inch distribution main plus a compressor station near Baldwin, in-service Dec. 2020), not FGT's interstate transmission loop from 2015-2017. Did not use it and flagging the name collision so a future pass doesn't accidentally cite it here.

verifications.note: WWALS Watershed Coalition (Suwannee Riverkeeper), Aug. 26, 2017: 'The Kinder Morgan (KMI) Jacksonville Expansion Project (JEP) of Florida Gas Transmission (FGT)'s natural gas pipelines...FERC permitted JEP (see FERC Docket Number CP15-144), and it has been built.' -- confirms construction complete by August 2017, consistent with recorded StartYear1=2017.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Single independent, non-GEM source pins completion to on-or-before Aug. 2017, matching the recorded 2017 start year, but gives no month. Searched for a second source with an exact in-service date (FERC in-service notification letter, an Energy Transfer/Kinder Morgan 10-K capex schedule, SEC EDGAR full-text search on 'Jacksonville Expansion') and found none -- FERC does not appear to post a stand-alone in-service filing for this docket on its public site, and neither company's SEC filings name this project specifically.

verifications.note: States the Jacksonville Expansion Project (FERC Docket CP15-144) 'has been built,' i.e., completed and placed in operation, as of Aug. 2017.
Current (2026) Energy Transfer pipeline-asset portal still lists 'Florida Gas Transmission' as an active system entity, i.e. the pipeline remains in operation today.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Two independent sources 9 years apart (2017 completion, 2026 still-listed-as-active) both consistent with recorded Status=operating.
